The response correctly identifies early January as the time of perihelion, when Earth is closest to the Sun at about 147 million km. The distance figures are accurate, and it rightly notes that this occurs in Northern Hemisphere winter, showing that distance does not cause the seasons. It also gives the real cause, the roughly 23.4-degree axial tilt. It stays well under 120 words and is clearly organized. It could have explained why the tilt matters more, but that is a minor gap given the answer is correct and the reasoning is sound.
